reviewer: AI assistant that also helped develop the system; not an independent or blinded expert
review_scope: Compare generated claims with the frozen retrieved abstracts and AI-assisted reference notes. Do not validate the papers' experimental results independently.
paired_prompts_verified: Each saved prompt pair differs only by the graph facts. Abstracts, question, instructions, model and generation options are shared.

summary.conclusion: No clear answer-quality benefit from adding graph facts on these five development questions. Graph-enriched generation took longer in this run. Both modes share a numerical interpretation error on the Bioformer case and usually omit source URLs.

cases.notes: Both explain query-rewriting optimization and accumulation of high-quality strategies to mitigate noisy feedback. The graph arm gives a more formal optimization description, but no essential additional answer fact. Neither answer includes a source URL.

cases.source_evidence: despite having about 40% of their parameters and producing 512-dimensional rather than 768-dimensional vectors
cases.notes: Both correctly state MAP +37.0% and Recall@100 +29.1%, and cite the correct paper. Both incorrectly turn 'about 40% of their parameters' into 'about 40% fewer parameters'. The source implies approximately 60% fewer parameters. The graph arm's extra claim about shorter vectors is supported.

Both identify pretrained CLIP text embeddings incorporated through AdaLN. The retrieval-only answer additionally mentions retained spherical sampling. Both answer the conditioning question correctly; neither provides a URL.

Answers are identical and explain optimizing a suffix to match steering-induced target activations instead of modifying hidden states at each generation step. They do not claim optimization itself requires no white-box access. Neither cites a URL. They omit concept-dependent effectiveness limits, so these short answers should not be taken as evidence of universal steering equivalence.
Both abstain rather than invent a current retail price. The retrieved abstracts do not provide that price. A source URL is not required for this pure abstention.

limitations: Only five English development cases; several were already used for debugging.
Each answerable question is primarily supported by one abstract, not a multi-hop graph task.
The shared retriever uses title identifiers plus vector search; retrieval_only means no graph facts, not removal of title-aware retrieval.
Scores are an AI-assisted qualitative review, not independent human annotations or a calibrated automatic judge.
Latency is one local run and includes caching/loading effects; it is not a statistically validated performance benchmark.
Temperature zero and a fixed seed do not guarantee identical results across runs.
